purpose: Eteplirsen is used to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients who have a specific change in their dystrophin gene that can benefit from skipping exon 51. DMD is a rare genetic disease that causes progressive muscle weakness. This medicine is for patients whose genetic test confirms they are eligible for this treatment.
how_it_works: Your muscles need a protein called dystrophin to stay healthy and strong. In DMD, a genetic mutation causes the body to make little or no working dystrophin. Eteplirsen works by 'skipping over' a faulty section of the genetic instructions (exon 51), allowing the body to produce a shorter but partially working version of dystrophin. Think of it like skipping a broken step on a staircase so you can still climb the stairs.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include balance problems, vomiting, skin rash or redness at the infusion site, upset stomach, nausea, and headache. Some patients may also experience upper respiratory infections or cough.
warnings: This medication is given through an IV (intravenous infusion) by a healthcare provider — you cannot take it at home on your own. There is a small risk of kidney problems, so your doctor will monitor your kidney function. Allergic reactions, including hives and skin redness, have been reported. Tell your doctor right away if you notice any unusual symptoms during or after your infusion. The FDA approved this drug under accelerated approval, meaning its full benefit is still being studied.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 30 mg per kilogram of body weight, given once a week as an intravenous (IV) infusion. The infusion is typically given over about 35 to 60 minutes in a clinic or hospital setting by a trained healthcare professional.
